heroHeadline: June 4 PLA All-Time Non-Exercise Record: 32 Sorties (25 Cross Median Line Into ALL FOUR ADIZ Sectors) on Tiananmen 37th Anniversary — Surpasses May 2 Prior Record (29); June 5 Post-Record Pullback: 7 Sorties SW ADIZ; Taiwan GDP Forecast 9.64% (16-Year High); Rubio: Arms Package 'Under Review,' Not Paused
heroSubtitle: On June 4, 2026, Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense recorded 32 PLA aircraft sorties — a new all-time non-exercise record surpassing May 2's prior peak of 29 — with 25 of 32 crossing the Taiwan Strait median line into all four ADIZ sectors simultaneously (northern, central, southwestern, eastern). Ten PLAN vessels and 5 official ships maintained maximum maritime pressure. The June 4 surge coincided with the 37th anniversary of Tiananmen Square: President Lai Ching-te called on China to 'face up to the June 4 incident, acknowledge the truth, and open the door to reconciliation and dialogue'; Taiwan held a candlelight vigil in Taipei. June 3 had already seen a re-escalation to 18 sorties (14/18 crossing N+SW ADIZ), two consecutive escalatory days after June 2's zero-crossing day. June 5 brought the predictable post-record pullback: 7 sorties (all SW ADIZ, zero median crossings), with 10 PLAN vessels and 6 ships sustaining elevated maritime presence. On June 3, Secretary Rubio testified before the Senate that the $14B Taiwan arms package (PAC-3/NASAMS) is 'under review' not paused, and the US does not consult Beijing on Taiwan arms decisions. Simultaneously, Computex 2026 (June 1-5) closed with Taiwan raising its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 9.64% — highest since 2010 — driven by AI demand; Nvidia's Jensen Huang announced up to $150B/year in Taiwanese supplier commitments. Full June sortie sequence: 7 (Jun 2) → 18 (Jun 3) → 32 RECORD (Jun 4) → 7 (Jun 5). Full extended sequence: 4→29→1→2→1→0→22→12→8→12→7→9→2→3→15→6→7→13→24→7→6→16→4→9→26→10→9→10→16→1→8→7→18→32→7. HIMARS NT$800M payment MET May 31; US FMS pause (Iran) active.
